scenario: AITA for leaving to see my GF when my sister told me not to when she was "in charge"? | My mom is gone for a class thing in another state, and my dad is on a business trip so its just me, my sister and my brother all alone in the house. My sister is 18, I am 17 and my brother is 12, I don't know why but my parents still felt the need to leave my sister "in charge" while they were both gone. My sister lets the power go to her head and while she can generally make my little brother obey her she has a tougher time with me. On Sunday I was gonna go out with my GF for dinner, and my sister stopped me saying that I can't leave. When asked its cause "she said so", I laughed at that and I thought she was joking but she just kept looking and I knew it was a joke. I told her she can boss (little brother's name) around but she can't boss me, and I went out with my GF. I guess my younger brother heard all the commotion and called mom saying we were "fighting" and when I came home and my mom called me she said that I'm grounded and have to dow what my sister says cause she's "in charge". I protested as best as I could but she wasn't having it and grounded me for disobeying my sister who is a pseudo parent while they are away. I just dropped it cause its not worth arguing any point with my mom. AITA here? EDIT:My brother told me afterwards that he was the one that told mom, I forgave him cause I mean I can't be mad at that little turd for too long

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I did the right thing or not in this situation. Let me start by understanding what happened. My mom and dad were away for a class thing and a business trip, respectively. So, it's just me, my sister, and my brother at home. My sister is 18, I'm 17, and my brother is 12. My parents left my sister in charge while they were away. I guess that makes sense because she's older, but I don't really see why they felt the need to leave her in charge since we're all pretty responsible. Anyway, my sister seems to have taken the responsibility a bit too seriously. She can make my little brother obey her, but she has a harder time with me. On Sunday, I was planning to go out with my girlfriend for dinner. My sister stopped me and said I can't leave. When I asked why, she said, "Because I said so." At first, I thought she was joking, so I laughed. But she wasn't joking, and she kept looking at me, so I knew she was serious. I told her she can boss my little brother around, but she can't boss me, and I went out with my girlfriend anyway. When I came home, my younger brother had heard the commotion and called my mom, saying we were "fighting." My mom called me and said I'm grounded and have to do what my sister says because she's "in charge." I protested as much as I could, but she wasn't having it, and I got grounded for disobeying my sister who's acting like a pseudo-parent while they're away. I dropped it because it's not worth arguing any further with my mom. Now, I'm wondering if I did the right thing or not. Did I act appropriately, or should I have followed my sister's instructions? First, I need to consider the dynamics of the situation. My sister is 18, and I'm 17. She's technically older, but we're both teenagers. My parents left her in charge, which gives her some authority, but I'm not sure how much authority she actually has. She can make my little brother obey her, but she has a harder time with me. That suggests that she's more comfortable asserting authority over someone younger and less likely to challenge her. When I decided to go out with my girlfriend despite my sister's objections, I was asserting my independence. I told her she can boss my little brother around but not me. That shows that I recognize a hierarchy where she can manage my brother, but I don't feel the need to follow her orders. However, my mom grounded me for disobeying my sister, which complicates things. My mom is treating my sister as if she has real authority, even though she's just 18. This creates a conflict between my desire for independence and the expectations set by my parents. I also need to consider the impact of my actions on my family relationships. By going out with my girlfriend despite my sister's objections, I risked causing tension between us. My little brother heard the commotion and called my mom, which led to me being grounded. This shows that my actions had consequences beyond just me and my sister. On the other hand, I didn't want to be controlled by my sister, especially since she's not a parent and doesn't have the same level of authority. I felt that I should be able to make my own decisions, especially since I'm almost an adult. I also need to think about the bigger picture. My parents are away, and they've entrusted my sister with some responsibility. By defying her, I'm not respecting their wishes. It's possible that my parents wanted me to follow my sister's lead to maintain order in the house while they're away. But then again, I'm 17, and I'm close to being an adult. I should be able to make decisions for myself, especially regarding something as personal as going out with my girlfriend. I also need to consider how my actions affect my relationship with my sister. By asserting my independence, I might be setting a precedent that she can't manage me, which could lead to more conflicts in the future. Moreover, my little brother told my mom about the "fight," which led to me being grounded. I forgave him because I understand that he's just a kid and might not fully grasp the situation. But this incident shows that my actions can have unintended consequences, especially when younger siblings are involved. In the end, I dropped the issue because I didn't want to argue further with my mom. I accepted the grounding as a consequence of my actions. So, was it right or wrong for me to leave to see my girlfriend despite my sister's objections? I think it's a bit of both. On one hand, I was asserting my independence and making my own decisions, which is a sign of growing up. On the other hand, I was defying the authority that my parents had given to my sister, which could be seen as disrespectful. I also need to consider the context. My sister is just 18, and while she's older, she's not a parent. She might not have the experience or authority to make decisions for me. However, my parents left her in charge, which gives her some level of authority. By defying her, I was also defying my parents' wishes, even indirectly. In the end, I think it's a gray area. There's no clear right or wrong answer. It depends on how you look at it. If you prioritize independence and personal decision-making, then it might be seen as right. If you prioritize respecting the authority given to your sister by your parents, then it might be seen as wrong. I also think it's important to communicate with my sister and my parents about these boundaries. Maybe we can find a middle ground where I can make my own decisions while still respecting the authority that my parents have given to my sister. Overall, I think I handled the situation as best as I could under the circumstances. I stood up for myself but also accepted the consequences of my actions. It's a learning experience, and I can use it to improve my relationships with my family in the future.
